newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain reports progress with China on HK issues.
newsitem.headline: Britain reports progress with China on HK issues.

text.p: Chinese and British negotiators working on details of Hong Kong's 1997 handover to Beijing began three days of talks on Wednesday and reached agreement on several issues, the British team leader said.

Britain's chief negotiator in the Joint Liaison Group (JLG) Hugh Davies told reporters after the meeting that the two sides agreed on a number of issues but he refused to identify the deals, saying they would be announced later.
"We had a very far-reaching discussion about many of the subjects which concern the transition," Davies told reporters.
"We have indeed managed to reach some agreements today. We are not going to tell you what those agreements are at this stage. They will be announced on the last day in a normal way," he said.
"We had a very full discussion...and we will continue our talks on all the JLG subjects over the next two days," he said.
China's team leader Zhao Jihua described the talks as "sincere, pragmatic and in-depth".
